cases.name: Ortralla "Tralla" LuWone Mosley
cases.about:
She was described as a good student, a cheerleader, a school dance-squad leader -- a responsible and thoughtful girl well liked by both students and teachers. "She was absolutely a shining star," said Vanessa Connor, Ortralla's English teacher, who was with her as she lay dying that Friday afternoon at the foot of a school stairway. "She was the person that a lot of students, particularly the girls, would go to when they were having problems. ... They really looked up to her."

Her mother Carolyn Mosley Samuel said, "She always said she liked butterflies because they are so free. She said, 'Momma, they're locked up in a cocoon, and then they're free,'" Carolyn remembers. "She lived a very full life, and I feel very satisfied -- that's what keeps me comfortable, knowing that her life was so satisfying to herself. So it wasn't the way that she died, it's the way that she lived, her legacy. The freedom that people have in their hearts -- building part of their lives on some of her strengths."

He stabbed her 6 times with two knives: once through the chest, into her heart; once through the back, piercing her left lung; once through the fleshy part on the back of her neck; once through the top of her skull into her brain and once on either side of her head, each thrust entering her brain through the temporal lobe. She had defensive wounds on her hands.

Ortralla then moved through the hallway doors and out onto the concrete second-floor walkway, at least another 20 feet to the top of a stairway, then down a flight of stairs, around a landing, and to the top of the lower flight of stairs, before losing her balance and collapsing, tumbling to the ground floor.

cases.name: Gloria Lofton
cases.about:
"She was a good lady, and she will watch out for the neighborhood," Sergio Rodriguez said.

Rodriguez had lived across the street from Lofton from the age of 10, up until her death. 

"I used to live with her before, too, to help out, pay bills and everything," Rodriguez said.

She helped him out, too, after Rodriguez's mom was murdered when he was only a child. He said she was a mother figure to him. 

"She was like a gangster mom," Rodriguez said. "She [would] always tells me, 'Stay in school, keep yourself straight,' you know. And I got a good job and everything because of her." 

This was all while Lofton had her own children.

Rodriguez said Lofton was sickly around the time of her death and, at one point, had cancer.
cases.narrative: A medical examiner labeled Lofton's death "undetermined" despite her being found with a strangulation mark on her neck and her shirt pulled above her head.

cases.name: Muriel Laverne Easley
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She had a dynamic personality, and was affectionately known as “Vernie” by family. Muriel accepted Christ into her life at an early age and joined Greater Mount Zion Baptist Church in Austin. A great conversationalist, she had a knack for being able to engage with virtually anyone. Her perspective was one of no-nonsense and straight-forwardness. She was warm, generous, very funny, attentive and deeply spiritual. She would always greet you with a broad smile and sparkly eyes that indicated that she was genuinely happy to see you.
She enjoyed spending time with friends and relatives, bible study, interacting with her grandchildren and listening to Gospel, R&B Oldies, Country and Pop music. She was admired as a devoted daughter, sister, wife, mother and grandmother. One of Muriel’s greatest attributes was that she lived with a Servant’s Heart. Whenever called upon for help, she would not hesitate to render whatever assistance she could. Frequently taking care of business transactions or running errands behind the scenes, she completed multitudes of thankless tasks with the express intent of honoring God.
She lived a highly organized and clean life of focus and determination. She graduated from the original L.C. Anderson High School in Austin, Tx. She later attended Huston-Tillotson University. This was followed by a 40-year career with the Texas Education Agency. She was a dedicated employee who rarely missed a day and was loved by her coworkers. She retired in 2003. Understanding that new parents are highly stressed, she jumped right back into service by volunteering to babysit her granddaughters, and making it easy for her daughter and new son-in-law.
On January 19, 2023, Muriel was called “Home” to be with our Father in Heaven. She shed the earthly bonds of this world, and answered the Master’s call to come and receive her well-deserved rest and reward. She was a true believer in Christ’s redemption and she ALWAYS spoke of the importance of faith. She fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith, and we know that she was received in Heaven with a mighty, “Well done, thou good and faithful servant.”"

cases.name: Shari Elaine Mallory Maxa
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "As 7th generation Daughter of the Republic of Texas, Shari was a God-fearing Texas Woman through and through. She was the oldest of three children born to Velma and Arnold Mallory in Waco, Texas. Shari grew up in Waco, Texas and left in 1959 to venture to El Paso, Texas for Arnold’s job. As she would say, they got to Austin as fast as they could. She attended Fulmore Junior High and William B Travis High School, class of 1967. Although their paths would soon cross again later in life, Shari and Tony met in high school and were dear friends through the years. Shari went on to attend Southwest Texas State University for one year before she married Jimmy Monaghan. The two shared two children, Jennifer Monaghan and James Austin Monaghan who were truly the greatest joys of her life. She was the proudest mom and even prouder grandmother. Shari never ceased to boast of all the accomplishments no matter how small her grandchildren and children obtained. Her love for UT came from Jennifer obtaining a degree from the University of Texas. She worked there for 18 years in the Student Records Section of the Chemistry and Biochemistry Department until she reached retirement. Her warm and loving smile impressed all the students she met during her tenure at UT.



Shari exuded so many traits of her mother – selfless, family first, loyal, and unconditionally loving. To say Shari loved family would be an understatement. At the time their paths crossed again, Shari met her soulmate, Anthony James Maxa aka Tony aka Papa aka the kindest man in the world. Shari poured her whole heart into her family and Tony gave all of his heart to her. The two of them tied the knot in 2005 in Coupland, Texas at her cousin, Larry’s dancehall. Shari gained another son, Bobby Maxa. The two of them blended their families beautifully and together they had three children, 10 grandchildren, and one great grandchild.



And although one would never see Shari without her French mani/pedi, they also never saw Shari without her beautiful smile. A smile that grew even bigger when she and Tony rekindled and married. The two of them were made for each other. Shari’s children considered Tony their parent and vice versa. There are not many strangers to Shari as she treated everyone she first met with the utmost kindness and generosity.



Shari’s impact was not only within her immediate family, but also in business. Now, of course, this was a family business. Shari joined her brother Randy Mallory in 2012 with his electrical company after she retired from UT. No one will ever be able to fill the void of Shari’s role at Malco. Every employee loved Shari as if she was a part of their family. There was no task too big or small that Shari would not resolve in order to take it off of Randy and Greg’s plate. Shari never forgot anyone’s birthday, and that included all of Malco’s employees. And as she’d admit, Shari was lucky to be surrounded by family every moment of her day. Many countless times, customers called to express their love and admiration working with Shari throughout the years. Whether it was when she was with her grandchildren and children or when she was working with her brothers, she took care of everyone.



Shari attended church at Columbus Baptist in Waco, Texas, and then became a member of Congress Avenue Baptist Church where she was baptized with her best friend Sharee Aery. After moving to Austin, Texas in 1962, the Mallory family joined Congress Avenue Baptist Church. Shari’s love for her family resembled Christ’s love for the church. As the bible instructs, Shari put on the full armor of Christ every day including at the moment of her untimely death. As of recent, she began attending church with her son and daughter and their respective families in Kyle, Texas. Her most recent honor was watching her daughter as well as her son’s children’s river baptism."

cases.name: Za’Riyah Marie Sheffield
cases.about:
"There's no other person out here in the whole world that's like Za'Riyah," her mother Wanakee White said. "She was the best thing in the world, like, for her to be taken ... I don't know."

Za'Riyah was a student at Connally High School who dreamed of working in business. Her aunt Neisha Sheffield has lost her voice from crying. "My baby not going to text me anymore. My life is going to be so different," Neisha Sheffield said. "He didn't just cheat my baby out of her life. He cheated her entire family, out of the best thing all of us have ever had."

Another aunt, Unique Bowser, is left clinging to Za'Riyah's memory. "To know her is to love her. And to know love," Bowser said. "Because that's all she was gonna give. That's all she giving to anybody."

Her obituary said, "Za’Riyah was a young teenager who loved everyone and always wanted to see her family happy. She always shared her smile and laughter with all those she loved and those who didn’t know her.
